newsitem.title: UK: Rolls drops after engine failure report.
newsitem.headline: Rolls drops after engine failure report.

text.p: Shares in Rolls Royce Plc dropped in early trading on Tuesday after a report in the Financial Times newspaper said the company could face compensation claims after turbine failures in some aero engines.
The stock was quoted down 5-1/2p at 238-1/2 at 0812 GMT GMT.
Analysts said the fact that Rolls had experienced some reliability problems was not in itself a huge surprise but it did emphasise the long-term risks of the aero engine business.

"It is not unduly surprising that they have had problems with engines over a period of time, but it is a reasonably big deal in as much as it points out that aero engines is a risky business," said one analyst who asked not to be named.
He said the adverse publicity could affect Rolls' reputation for technical reliability, though rivals had also had problems.

"There is an element of risk for the shares which we don't feel is being discounted several years ahead," he said, adding that it remained to be seen whether any compensation claims were actually lodged.

The FT said the problems, affecting a version of its RB211 engine, had caused some in-flight engine shut-downs, though it said Rolls argued that it was not unusual for airlines to experience similar problems on engines from all manufacturers.
